chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Yazid ibn Khalifah, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: Indeed, 'Umar ibn Hanzalah came to us from you regarding a time. So Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: Then he does not lie against us.
So I said: He mentioned that you say that the first time of a salat (prayer) which Allah, Exalted is He, made obligatory upon His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is the noon prayer.
And it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Establish the salat (prayer) at the declining of the sun.”

So when the sun passes the meridian, nothing prevents you except your supererogatory prayer. Then you remain within the time until the shadow becomes one stature, and that is the end of the time. So when the shadow becomes one stature, the time of the afternoon prayer enters, and you remain within the time of the afternoon prayer until the shadow becomes two statures, and that is the evening.
He said: He spoke the truth.

key_terms.الظُّهْرُ: the noon prayer, identified here as the first obligatory prayer time of the day
key_terms.الظِّلُّ: the shadow, used here as a measure for prayer times
key_terms.دُلُوكِ: the declining of the sun from the meridian
key_terms.زَالَتِ: passed the zenith; declined from the middle of the sky
key_terms.وَقْتٍ: appointed time for performing the prayer

ai.seo_question: When do the times of zuhr and 'asr prayers begin and end according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal timings of the zuhr and 'asr prayers and affirms a report transmitted by 'Umar ibn Hanzalah. It also cites the Qur'anic phrase about establishing salat (prayer) at the declining of the sun as evidence for the beginning of the prayer time, making the narration important in Shia jurisprudence on prayer times.
